Astarion is enjoying himself at a party with the goblins. You've betrayed and slaughtered the tieflings and he's finally able to indulge his hedonistic side. He's drinking blood, but offers you wine. He or you can propose that you get together tonight and enjoy a little more hedonism when everyone else is asleep.

Following a trail of whispered ADs ('Psst. Over here!' 'Come on, before it's too late!') we find a pale elf, hunched down near some long grass. He insists an intellect devourer (brain monster with legs) is hiding there, trying to cajole you to look and kill it. If you approach the grass, a boar bursts out - it was a distraction while Astarion got behind you. He's on edge, but pleased to have the jump on you. He holds a blade to your throat while demanding you tell him what happened on the ship. After a mind meld (vision where he sees a glimpse of your past) you can convince him that you're both victims and should work together to find an answer. Once he realises you're not a threat his tone changes from threatening to charming.
A disguised Viconia approaches the player and sits down beside them. They will ask questions to uncover the depths of their psyche. Before potentially inviting them to enter the Grotto.
Players AD after an Arcana check when they are inside the Diabolist House and see devilish objects.
context: The party has been intercepted by a devil — Raphael — who appeared, taunted the group, and spirited everyone off to the House of Hope for a dinner meeting. Gale, who has studied fiends extensively though never met one in person, smelled the infernal signs and suspects the devil is hiding his desperation behind bluster. He warns the devil is likely angling for something grave (he even names "souls" as the likely opening offer) but argues that the devil’s eagerness might be exploitable. The player is cautious about bargains and asks how to outmaneuver a devil without taking an obvious short straw.
